clue.text: Morgan pranged against English tree

indicators.note: to prang is British slang for crashing a car, so the name is smashed up and rearranged

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against

explanation.surface: Someone called Morgan has crashed their car into a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pranged' signals the anagram; to prang is British slang for a minor car crash, which suits the surface perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tropical species that grows in coastal swamps, an example of the category named.

clue.text: Period hard to recall due to insanity?

definitions.text: Period hard to recall due to insanity?

parts.words: Period hard to recall due to insanity?
parts.note: the phrase means a past so distant nobody remembers it, but read literally it suggests a stretch spent mad and so forgotten

explanation.surface: A spell of time you cannot remember because you had lost your reason.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: the idiom for the immemorial past is read as a period of being crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes ages beyond memory, which is exactly a period too remote to recall.

clue.text: Explosive cavalry assault

definitions.meaning: an explosive used in blasting or a gun is a quantity of powder, the noun sense
horsemen rushing at the enemy, as in the Light Brigade's famous attack

explanation.surface: A cavalry attack described as explosive in its force.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a measured load of explosive and a headlong mounted attack: two separate senses.

clue.text: Expert's witticism spoken in French

parts.note: a pun is a joke playing on words, a kind of witticism
dit is the French for said or spoken

explanation.surface: A specialist's clever quip delivered in French.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Expert's' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A commentator called in to give authoritative opinions is a recognised specialist, a synonym.

clue.text: Soldier on airplane ordered to carry hot gear

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

indicators.note: one thing carries another by holding it within, so H goes inside
the letters of the word are put in a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A paratrooper loads hot kit aboard a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' is the anagram signal and 'to carry' the container signal; 'on' just places the soldier first in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means miscellaneous equipment and belongings, which is a loose synonym for kit.

clue.text: Amount to nothing in Japanese sport

parts.note: a sum is an amount
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Something adds up to nothing in a sport from Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of heavyweight wrestling is Japan's national sport, an example of the category.

clue.text: Capital H for church district

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

explanation.surface: A capital letter H used as a symbol for a church district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like it describes H as an upper-case letter; in fact it is a city, and H is simply given as written.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the area served by one church and its priest, a direct synonym.

clue.text: World University managed by American

parts.note: ran, as one runs a business, means managed
US stands for American, as in US forces

explanation.surface: A world university run by an American.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventh planet from the Sun is a world in the astronomical sense, an example of one.

clue.text: Giant making some progress

indicators.note: only some of the word's letters are wanted, a run buried within it

explanation.surface: A giant who is getting on a bit with something.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eating giant of fairy tales, so the monster is an example of a giant.

clue.text: Heater that's cooler for car

definitions.meaning: a household panel through which hot water flows to warm a room
the part of an engine that sheds heat from the coolant

explanation.surface: Something that warms you yet also cools a car engine.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the contrast: one object warms a room, the same name cools an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a room-warming panel and an engine's heat exchanger, two opposite jobs.

clue.text: Greek character in short time creates shrine

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a moment is a short time
nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek figure who builds a shrine in no time.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorial structure honouring someone can serve as a shrine, a near synonym.

clue.text: Badger in range occasionally

indicators.note: taking letters only now and then, every other one of these words

explanation.surface: A badger roaming within its territory now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' looks like the animal; it is the verb meaning pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester them persistently, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Pirate shot by cricketer

definitions.meaning: Captain ..., the villain of Peter Pan
a cross-batted stroke pulling a short ball to the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A pirate shot dead by a cricket player.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket this is a stroke played across the line to a short, rising ball.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the name of Peter Pan's piratical captain and of a cricket stroke: two distinct senses.

clue.text: Oily formulation spilled on mitten

indicators.note: things spilled are scattered in disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Some greasy cream knocked over onto a glove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilled' rearranges the letters of ON MITTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A greasy salve rubbed on the skin is an oily preparation, a descriptive synonym.

clue.text: Somewhat insane Roman?

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is taken, a run of their letters

explanation.surface: A rather unhinged Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'insane Roman', and the whole clue describes the emperor famed for madness.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor, notorious for his cruelty and erratic behaviour, fits a mad Roman.

clue.text: Ringo roused worker maybe in the dark

indicators.note: stirred up, so the name's letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: an ant is the crossword's typical worker, from the worker ants of a colony

explanation.surface: Ringo wakes up a labourer who may know nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roused' signals the anagram of the Beatle's name; 'maybe' warns that the ant is only one example of a worker.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the dark about something is an idiom for being uninformed or unaware.

clue.text: The writer joins cool firm for salary

parts.note: in means fashionable or cool
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
the setter refers to themself, so the writer is me

explanation.surface: An author signs up with a trendy company for a wage.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings received for work, so a salary is one kind of this, a near synonym.

clue.text: Victorious flag officer in the hold

definitions.meaning: Horatio, the admiral who won at Trafalgar in his flagship Victory
a wrestling grip applied from behind under the arms and up to the neck

explanation.surface: A winning admiral below deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victorious' puns on HMS Victory, the admiral's flagship; 'hold' suggests a ship's hold but is a wrestling grip.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to Britain's great admiral and to a wrestling grip: two separate senses.

clue.text: One may react with surprising malice after church

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the church abbreviation
surprising here works as a verb, catching the letters off guard and scrambling them

explanation.surface: Someone reacts to unexpected spite after a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprising' is the anagram signal, read as a verb acting on the spite; 'after' puts the church abbreviation first.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance in chemistry takes part in reactions, so it is something that may react.

clue.text: Old banger worth little has top missing

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: something cheap is of little value

explanation.surface: A clapped-out car, almost worthless, with its roof gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has top missing' removes the C from CHEAP. A banger is British slang for a battered old car.
explanation.definitionFit: This is slang for a dilapidated car, the same thing as a battered old motor.

clue.text: Culminating point of month in service

parts.note: an ace is a serve the opponent cannot touch in tennis

explanation.surface: The high point of a month spent in someone's service.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the summit or peak of achievement, a synonym for the high point.

clue.text: Mother keeps silver with note in bottle

indicators.note: the mother holds the other letters inside her

parts.note: mum is an informal word for mother
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Mum hoards her silver together with a note inside a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large wine bottle holding twice the standard amount, a type of bottle.

clue.text: Whence gold that is associated with scripture?

definitions.text: Whence gold that is associated with scripture?

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
NT is the New Testament, scripture

explanation.surface: Asks where the gold mentioned in the Bible came from.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue nods to the Magi, who came from the East bearing gold in the Gospel story.
explanation.definitionFit: The East, poetically named, is where the wise men of scripture set out from with gold.
